text:
Alyssa: Quick follow-up from today's RFC review — we need a concrete contract for midstream handoff when the gateway hedges/fallbacks an ongoing streaming call. Two main concerns: 1) ordering/dedupe of tokens produced by old vs new upstreams, 2) SLO & billing attribution for partial/overlapping attempts. Thoughts?

Mike: +1 on explicit seq checkpoints. I think two lightweight things suffice: a monotonic `X-Stream-Seq` header on token frames and an opaque `X-Resume-Token` you can hand to a new upstream. New upstream would start with `resume_at=seq+1`.

Sophia: Edge case — if the client has already seen part of a token window and the gateway retries, duplication gets visible to client SDKs. We should consider client-visible checkpoint markers so SDKs can ignore duplicates (or drop them server-side). :thinking:

Kevin: We can't update SDKs everywhere quickly. Prefer gateway-side suppression: gateway assigns a monotonic per-request message-id and drops duplicates before forwarding downstream. Simpler for rollout.

Alyssa: Implementation sketch: emit explicit checkpoint frames in the stream like `type=checkpoint` that include `seq` and `resume_token`. Gateway treats checkpoint as a commit point. Resume semantics: new upstream uses `resume_token` to advance KV/seq state. Example frame (pseudo-JSON):
```json
{ "type": "checkpoint", "seq": 12345, "resume_token": "b64..." }
```
This sits inline with token frames.

Mike: This is like trailers but midstream. Concern: generating resume tokens frequently may force us to flush lots of KV state (bandwidth/latency cost). Maybe only emit checkpoints on explicit upstream switch events or at semantic boundaries (sentence/paragraph).

Sophia: For billing/SLO: we should ensure attribution is clear — accepted/committed tokens are what the customer is billed for, but hedged attempts may still consume backend cycles we index internally. Suggest: external billing = committed tokens; internal metrics increment both attempted tokens and committed tokens. Need hooks in billing pipeline.

Alyssa: Agreed. Proposal summary: (1) Gate emits midstream `checkpoint` frames at either semantic boundaries or on upstream switch. (2) Gateway dedupes duplicates using monotonic message IDs before forwarding to client. (3) Observability emits events `stream.attempt.started`, `stream.checkpoint.committed`, `stream.attempt.abandoned` for billing & debugging.

Kevin: Operational note: we can implement commit semantics with a tiny per-request in-memory commit log (TTL'd). On failover the new upstream asks control-plane RPC for the last committed `seq` for that request id to hydrate resume state. Keep the log tiny and ephemeral (e.g., 30s TTL).

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout scheduled for edge-proxy v1.12.0 tomorrow @0400 UTC. Feature flag `enable_midstream_checkpoints` will gate this behavior.

Alyssa: Decision check — do we agree to: (A) midstream checkpoint frames (sentence boundaries / upstream switch), (B) gateway-side dedupe/suppression, (C) observability events + billing attribution design doc? Vote please.

Mike: :+1:

Sophia: :+1: I'll draft the billing/observability doc and include example metrics and event schemas.

Kevin: :+1: I'll prototype the commit log + resume RPC in the proxy.

Alyssa: Thanks all — I'll file the follow-up RFC with API sketches for the checkpoint frame, the resume RPC, and billing hooks.
